sections.html:
Hurry changes the math in Redmond. You can accept a cash offer, hire a listing agent, or run the sale yourself, and the right choice follows your calendar, the house's condition and your appetite for spending before closing.

Redmond sits in King County about 15 miles east of Seattle, with 82,506 residents counted in July 2025. Buyers here are tied to the tech economy around the Microsoft campus. Homes steps from the Overlake or downtown light rail stops can pull a different buyer pool from those on Education Hill or the outer streets. Start by ranking your priorities:

  • A guaranteed closing day, perhaps tied to a relocation, a new job or a probate clock.
  • Top dollar, which normally calls for repairs, staging and several weeks of showings.
  • A clean handoff of everything as it is, furniture, postponed maintenance and unpermitted work included.

A cash buyer needs no loan approval, so title work and your own plans mostly set the timeline. Ask every bidder to put price, closing day, who pays which costs and any repair credit on paper, then compare the offers side by side.

Over half of Redmond households rent. Plenty of sellers are therefore retired landlords or heirs who inherited a rental, and the permit and short-term rental notes below may apply to you.

Housing measureRedmond, 2020 to 2024
Median value of owner-occupied homes$1,167,800
Households living in a home they own43.2%
Median gross rent$2,409
Median household income$162,560

Medians blend condos with big lots. For a real read on your house, look at what sold recently close to your address.

Median rent of $2,409 a month is worth noting if you are weighing whether to keep a rental or sell it.

Overlake, southwest of downtown, holds the Microsoft headquarters plus apartments and houses. Education Hill lies north of downtown. New construction has concentrated downtown and in Overlake, both on the 2 Line light rail. That line's first stretch began service in April 2024, and trains reached Downtown Redmond on May 10, 2025.

Nearly all of Redmond is in the Lake Washington School District. The southernmost blocks, mainly below NE 40th Street, fall under the Bellevue School District, and the unincorporated English Hill area belongs to Northshore. Buyers filter listings by district, so put yours in the description.

sections.h2: What the state disclosure form covers
sections.html:
Washington's seller disclosure form digs into water problems and construction history, and buyers study your answers. Expect prompts like these:

  • Any roof leak in the past five years.
  • Basement flooding or leaking, standing water, or drainage trouble.
  • Whether permits and final inspections exist for additions, conversions or remodels.
  • Critical areas, wetlands or floodplains on the lot.

RCW 64.06.020 sets the timing. The signed form reaches the buyer within five business days of a mutually accepted written contract, unless both sides agree to something else. After delivery the buyer gets three business days to back out, unless that right was waived. Sellers must also supply a smoke detector and install carbon monoxide alarms where the state building code requires them.

Redmond expects a building permit before you add on, remodel, convert a garage, build a deck or create an accessory dwelling unit. A few jobs need none: a one-story detached accessory structure up to 200 square feet, a retaining wall no higher than 4 feet, and window replacement within existing openings. Newly built homes and detached accessory dwelling units need fire sprinklers.

Built something without a permit? Put it on the disclosure form. An as-is cash sale lets you hand the house over without finishing the paperwork, though the buyer will discount the price for the risk. Development Services can show you what is on file under your address.

Short-term rental rules are recent. Ordinance 3239 (December 2, 2025) created a Redmond business license for short-term rentals, effective January 1, 2026, in addition to the state license. One license is issued per rental address in single-family zones, and one per operator in multifamily or mixed-use buildings. Stays under 30 consecutive nights are covered. An owner-occupied home renting fewer than three rooms for at least six months a year is outside the definition. Running without a license brings a penalty of 100 percent of the fee, so check your standing before you transfer a working rental.

A short visit to Development Services can save a deal. Bring your street address and any permit numbers or contractor invoices from past additions, a finished basement or a garage conversion. Ask whether each project has a final inspection on file, and whether a detached accessory unit meets the sprinkler requirement.

Write down what you learn and keep it with your sale folder. A buyer's inspector is likely to raise the same questions, and a clear answer from the city is stronger than your memory of what a contractor did years ago.

If you find a gap, you have two choices. You can finish the permit work yourself before listing, or you can sell as-is and disclose the gap so the offer reflects it.

Washington's real estate excise tax normally lands on the seller. Payment goes to the treasurer of the county where the property sits, and the Department of Revenue counts the notarized deed date as the sale date. The state share is tiered and a local share is added. Starting with sales on January 1, 2027, the tiers are:

  • 1.1% up to $551,000
  • 1.28% from $551,000 to $1,551,000
  • 2.75% from $1,551,000 to $3,051,000
  • 3.0% over $3,051,000

Ask your escrow officer or the King County Recorder's Office for the local share on a Redmond address, and for the tiers that apply if you close before the new year. Late payment starts accruing interest one month after the sale, and the Department of Revenue shows an assessment rate of 6 percent for 2026.

A separate property tax bill also follows the parcel. Its due date is April 30 (RCW 84.56.020), and a total of $50 or more may be paid in two halves, the second by October 31. At closing the agent divides the year's amount between you and the buyer. King County Treasury can supply a current statement before you commit to a date.

Every path swaps something for something else.

  • Agent listing: broad Eastside exposure, plus showings, inspections and repair haggling.
  • Do-it-yourself sale: no commission, but you take on marketing, the disclosure form, the contract and the excise tax affidavit.
  • As-is cash sale: fewer moving parts and a date of your choosing, with a price that reflects condition.

Pull together the same folder in every case: the deed, a loan payoff statement if you owe, permit records, HOA documents for an association home, and the newest property tax statement.

A cash deal can move briskly. After you accept, escrow opens and title is searched. Any mortgage is cleared out of your proceeds. Signing happens before a notary, the affidavit and tax reach the county, and funds are released after the deed is recorded. Nobody orders an appraisal or lender review, so repairs you never made fall to the buyer, who has already priced them in.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale take in Redmond, WA?
faqs.a: Title work and the buyer decide it, so request the closing date in writing. Without an appraisal or loan underwriting, a cash deal usually wraps up sooner than a financed listing, though your own payoff or probate step can slow it.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Redmond sale?
faqs.a: The seller, normally. Payment goes to the county treasurer by the sale date. If the seller skips it, liability shifts to the buyer and a lien can attach. Escrow works out the state and local portions.

faqs.q: Must I hand a Redmond buyer the disclosure form?
faqs.a: Yes for most improved residential sales, unless the buyer waives it or RCW 64.06.010 exempts the transfer. Deliver it within five business days of an accepted written contract. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Redmond house with unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, and the work should be disclosed. The state form asks about permits and final inspections for additions and remodels, and an as-is buyer will reflect that in the offer. Development Services can show what is on file.

faqs.q: Does a former short-term rental need a license before I sell?
faqs.a: Selling needs no license. The requirement, in force since January 1, 2026, applies to operating a qualifying short-term rental. If yours ran unlicensed, ask the city about a penalty before closing.
